title: Diameter of Binary Tree
description:
Given the `root` of a binary tree, return the **length of the diameter** of the tree.

The **diameter** of a binary tree is the length of the longest path between any two nodes in the tree, measured by the **number of edges** between them. This path may or may not pass through the `root`. For a single-node tree, the diameter is `0`.
hints: For any node, the longest path that bends at that node has length `height(node.left) + height(node.right)` edges.
Remember that the overall diameter does not have to pass through the root — it could lie entirely inside a left or right subtree.
Compute subtree heights in a single post-order DFS while updating a global maximum diameter at every node to achieve O(n) time.

examples.explanation: The longest path is 4 -> 2 -> 1 -> 3 (or 5 -> 2 -> 1 -> 3), which has 3 edges.
The longest path is 1 -> 2, which has 1 edge.
A tree with a single node has no edges, so its diameter is 0.
